notes:
CIRCUIT: the same multi-stage discrete transistor network as circuit_43, redrawn by the same hand (9 BJTs, 6 resistors, 2 diodes, 5 single-port supply arrows +15V/+10V/+6V/+5V/+3V). NOTE: this sheet has NO GND symbol, so there is no net named '0'; the bottom rail at y~855 is an ordinary net (n15 here). 22 components, 16 nets.

No GND symbol is drawn anywhere on this sheet, so this net gets an ordinary name.
  n16 = base of Q#19 (293,785) east to the base of Q#20 (409,783). Only 2 terminals; re-traced the whole y~784 run at 4x and nothing else touches it - the drafter drew a bare base-to-base tie (identical to the same feature in circuit_43).

JUDGEMENT CALLS (sites):
  - S4 (733,508) deg=4, CRITICAL, tracer default junction (kind=plainX-junction, dot=1.1, hop=4.6): OVERRIDDEN TO CROSSING. At 4x and in the site crop the x~725 diode column makes an unmistakable smooth S-shaped SIDEWAYS JOG - it bends right to x~735 above the rail, passes the y~508 horizontal, then bends back left to x~720 and continues down to D#10. The horizontal runs dead straight through the middle of the bow. On this sheet a jog means 'not connected'. Branches pair as (e14 up, e20 down) and (e17 left, e18 right). Consequence of the other reading: D#4's cathode, D#10's anode, R#8's right end, Q#2's emitter, the +5V arrow, Q#13's emitter and Q#17's collector would collapse into ONE 7-terminal net, shorting out the series-diode midpoint and destroying net n5 entirely.
  - S22 (564,792) deg=4, CRITICAL, tracer default junction (dot=1.5, hop=5.9): OVERRIDDEN TO CROSSING. Same gesture: the R#15 (50k) column comes down at x~553, bows right to x~568, passes the y~790 horizontal and returns to x~562 on its way to the bottom rail at S26. The horizontal carries Q#12's collector / Q#20's collector across to Q#18's base. Junction here is what produced the tracer's absurd 10-terminal net n11, in which Q#18 had base AND emitter on the same net and Q#20 had collector AND emitter on the same net - both transistors shorted out. Crossing removes both shorts and splits the node into the signal net n11 (3 terminals) and the bottom rail n15 (7 terminals), which is exactly the count the identical circuit_43 has.
  - S5 (812,509) deg=4 CRITICAL, dot=1.8, hop=5.7: JUNCTION. The crop shows a clean plain X with NO jog and a modestly thickened centre, sitting 80px from S4 where the same drafter did draw a jog. Same-sheet habit is decisive: they jog when they mean 'not connected', so a bare crossing here is a real tie. Consequence of crossing: the +5V arrow and R#8's right end would be a 2-terminal net while Q#2's emitter, Q#13's emitter and Q#17's collector formed another - contradicted by the absent jog and by the matching junction in circuit_43 (site S29 there, which carries an unambiguous solder blob).
  - S6 (462,515) deg=4 CRITICAL, dot=2.0, hop=5.7: JUNCTION. Plain X, no jog; the +6V shaft runs straight down through the resistor chain to Q#12's emitter. Crossing would strand the +6V arrow with only Q#12's emitter and cut the 150ohm/15k chain in half. The matching site in circuit_43 (S16) carries a clear solder dot; here dot=2.0 is the joint-highest reading on the sheet.
  - S1 (562,258), S3 (254,380), S7 (258,521), S8 (811,591), S14 (714,658), S18 (448,698), S24 (702,850), S26 (554,856), S27 (166,856), S28 (248,856), S29 (452,856) - all CRITICAL, all JUNCTION. Every one of these crops shows a T (or a T plus a collinear continuation), i.e. a lead terminating on a through-running wire, so 'crossing' cannot even be expressed; the only alternative, 'none', would float a lead or break the bottom rail. S27 (dot=2.2) and S8/S24/S26/S29 (dot=2.0) additionally carry visible blobs. Recorded explicitly to document that each was inspected.
  - Non-critical sites S0, S9, S12, S15, S16, S17, S20, S23 were inspected in the montages: S0/S9/S12 are self-intersections of the '+15V' and '+3V' captions, S16/S17/S20/S23 are the '50 kohm' captions and resistor zigzag ink. S15 (69,693) is the real +3V T-junction and its default (junction) is correct - it is what net n14 hangs on. All left at defaults.

PORT FIXES:
  - VDC#14 (+3V): t0 was bound to p0 (49,621), a stroke of the arrowhead/caption above the symbol, giving the 1-terminal net n13. Re-bound to p1 (69,681), the foot of the arrow shaft, which joins the +3V T at S15 together with Q#16's base and R#21's top. The other four supply arrows (#0 +15V, #3 +10V, #6 +6V, #7 +5V) were already correctly bound to their feet and were left alone.
  - PIN ORDER, all four BJT-PNPs (#11, #12, #13, #16): the tracer assumed emitter = bottom lead everywhere. On this sheet, as on circuit_43, every PNP is drawn with the EMITTER on the UPPER lead. Verified at 10x on #12 and #13 and at 4x on #11 and #16: the arrowhead sits on the upper lead with its barbs opening away from the base bar and its point landing ON the base bar (arrow pointing INTO the base = PNP emitter); the lower lead is plain. Applied (collector, base, emitter): #11 -> (p1 bottom, p2 left, p0 top); #12 -> (p2 bottom, p1 right, p0 top); #13 -> (p2 bottom, p1 left, p0 top); #16 -> (p0 bottom, p1 left, p2 top).
  - All five BJT-NPNs (#2, #17, #18, #19, #20) were checked and are already correct: arrowhead on the LOWER lead pointing AWAY from the base bar, so (collector, base, emitter) = (top, side, bottom) as the tracer had it. No change.
  - Ignored port candidates: R#1's p2 (234,302) is the 'V' of the '+10V' caption brushing the box; R#21's p1/p2/p4 (~(87,780-800)) are strokes of the '50 kohm' caption. The tracer had already declined to use any of them, which is correct.

CLASSES: all 22 symbols match their labels; PNP vs NPN is confirmed by arrow direction on every transistor and agrees with the COCO classes. Both diodes are drawn triangle-down with the bar below (anode up, cathode down). No re-classification needed.

UNRESOLVED / NOTED: (a) there is no GND symbol on this sheet, so no net is named '0' - the bottom rail n15 is just another net. (b) nets n5 (D#4/D#10 midpoint) and n16 (Q#19/Q#20 base tie) each have only 2 terminals; both are genuine features of the drawing and both appear identically in circuit_43, which is the same schematic drawn a second time. (c) All 16 gap bridges were reported as netlist-neutral and were left alone. ERC clean: 22 components, 16 nets, every terminal assigned; the resulting netlist is isomorphic to the one I derived independently for circuit_43, which is a strong cross-check.
